`antitrust` separates the **structural lifecycle** from the existing
model-specific S4 economics. This lets users fit once and run controlled
scenarios while keeping the result classes and methods that economic models
already implement. The [workflow vignette](Workflow.html) demonstrates that
lifecycle; the [models vignette](Models.html) describes its FOCs and
identification assumptions.

## Objects in the lifecycle

```text
model_spec() + observed inputs  --calibrate()-->  AntitrustFit
model_spec() + known parameters --specify()---->  AntitrustFit
AntitrustFit + Counterfactual --simulate()---->  legacy S4 result (one step)
AntitrustFit + multiple steps --simulate()----->  CounterfactualPath
```

`model_spec()` normalizes a supported demand, conduct and variant identity.
An `AntitrustFit` is a `StructuralFit`: it stores that identity, an existing
fitted model object, structural parameters, observed inputs and diagnostics.
It marks the state *before* a requested counterfactual. A
`Counterfactual` contains one or more `CounterfactualStep` objects. One step
returns the existing model class, such as `Logit`, `CES`, `Cournot`, or
`Auction2ndLogit`; a multi-step simulation returns `CounterfactualPath`,
whose `result_at()` and `final_result()` return those same model classes.

This choice preserves the economic methods already defined for result
classes. A universal result class would lose model-specific dispatch and
would force unrelated auction, quantity-game and bargaining outputs into one
set of slots. `summary(fit)` describes stored fit state;
`summary(result)` describes the simulation under the result class's method.

## S4 relationships that affect behavior

The following is a deliberately selective map of *current* inheritance.
Arrows mean “extends”; they do not assert that two economic games share a
FOC. Some descendants inherit demand storage and override supply methods.

```text
StructuralFit (virtual)
  └─ AntitrustFit

Antitrust
  ├─ Bertrand
  │   ├─ Linear ── LogLin, AIDS ── PCAIDS ── PCAIDSNests
  │   ├─ Logit ── LogitNests, LogitCap, LogitCournot, LogitBLP,
  │   │             Auction2ndLogit, BargainingLogit, MonComLogit
  │   ├─ CES ── CESNests, CESCournot, Auction2ndCES,
  │   │           BargainingCES, MonComCES
  │   └─ Cournot ── Stackelberg
  └─ Auction2ndCap

Counterfactual ── contains CounterfactualStep objects
CounterfactualPath ── contains legacy S4 results
```

The diagram omits ALM, nested, BLP and auction/bargaining subvariants where
they do not change this explanation. `Cournot`'s inheritance from
`Bertrand` is an implementation inheritance, not a claim that Cournot uses
Bertrand price FOCs. The former `ClassDiagram.png` omitted the new lifecycle
and several result families; `methods::showClass()` and
`methods::showMethods()` give the authoritative detailed hierarchy.

## Public methods and dispatch

The current public price and margin generics are `calcPrices()` and
`calcMargins()` (there are no exported `prices()` or `margins()` generics).
Results also support, where their class defines a method,
`calcShares()`, `calcQuantities()`, `elast()`, `diversion()`, `upp()`,
`cmcr()`, `CV()`, `HypoMonTest()`, and `calcDiagnostics()`. For example,
`elast()` on a `Logit` result and on a `CES` result dispatches to their
respective demand equations. See each generic's help page for argument
conventions; availability is not identical across all model classes.

The model registry behind `supportedModels()` records **complete supported
implementations**: normalized identity, existing S4 result class, legacy
calibration constructor, and support for `calibrate()`, `specify()` and
`simulate()`. It does not mechanically cross every demand family with every
conduct family. Each entry delegates economic behavior to its model-specific
constructor and methods. A second, narrower transition registry controls
`respecify()` and records what is retained, derived, discarded and
recomputed. `model_transition()` exposes those records for supported
source/target specifications.

The public `counterfactual()` vocabulary is broader than any one model.
`validate_counterfactual()` checks fields against model-specific
capabilities before solving. In particular, entry, quality, capacity,
bargaining and leadership are conditional capabilities; tariff and quota
are rejected for antitrust models.

## Building an extension

An extension package should own its **specialized economics**: model
identities beyond `antitrust::supportedModels()`, calibration equations,
equilibrium solves, and result methods. It can reuse exported lifecycle
types and hooks when appropriate: subclass `StructuralFit`, implement
`simulate()` and `respecify()` for its own fit class, validate its
counterfactual fields, and implement `simulate_steps()` if paths should
resume. The generic `StructuralFit` methods fail explicitly until the
extension supplies behavior; they do not silently run antitrust economics.

The sibling packages show distinct uses of this boundary. `vertical` owns
two-sided vertical bargaining models and their policy state. `coordination`
owns specialized price-leadership economics. `trade` depends on antitrust
and adds tariff/quota policy rather than moving generic market design out of
antitrust. `financial` supplies its own debt/limited-liability lifecycle.
`antitrustBayes` can construct antitrust fits from posterior structural
draws and use the public simulation boundary. These are architectural
examples, not a claim that all packages share one registry.

`synthetic_market()`, `fake_market()`, and `realize_market()` also belong to
antitrust: neutral market design and model-specific realization are separate
parts of antitrust's public synthetic-market tools. Extensions can consume
the resulting structural fits while retaining responsibility for their own
economic validity.

For a downstream package, the dependable integration surface is the
exported functions, documented S4 classes, documented result generics, and
their stated argument contracts. Do not use `antitrust:::` registry helpers,
promotion functions, solver state or unnamed attributes as extension
contracts. In the source repository, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and
`artifacts/refactor_architecture.md` contain maintainer context;
`?StructuralFit`, `?AntitrustFit`, `?simulate_steps` and
`?validate_counterfactual` define the callable hooks.
